scope: Connected io_uring maintenance-state ownership: original mm/task admission, pending publication, background progress, waits, external work classification, legacy escalation, cancellation and retirement.

architecture.identity: Original (Memory instruction owner, task) scope, independent of shared ring FD numbers and foreign CQ visibility.
architecture.state: Actor-wide active/revision/owner-required fields are removed. One relaxed atomic per scope holds pending, legacy-required and publication generation. Original ring/resource locks still publish request bytes.
architecture.stale_publication: Idle or legacy-progress acknowledgement compares the observed generation. A later pending publication cannot be erased by an old completion.
architecture.production: Linux clone_with_resources already creates a separate actor per task. These multi-origin regressions cover reused/embedding actors and do not establish a common-workload global-actor bottleneck.
architecture.fast_path: One origin uses a retained OnceLock scope, without a registry lock or tree lookup. Only secondary origins use the object-local cold registry. No per-SQE body lock, per-byte/per-instruction check, new guest fence or algorithm-level serialization is added.
architecture.lifetime: Pending work pins a secondary scope; retained observers preserve its identity across reactivation. Last inactive observer drop removes its weak registry entry. The first scalar scope lives until its actor retires. Scopes retain no Files, guest memory/task or strong ring.
architecture.external: Accepted FileIo records original owner/task; pending native jobs classify only that submitter as external. Poll/enter/background paths use the same identity.
architecture.legacy: Both real missing-native-wait and deferred-body escalation setters remain and now mark their original scope. The actual worker stop/join boundary remains; it has not been renamed as removed.
